chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, a man will come on the Day of Resurrection with him the measure of a cup of blood, so he will say, 'By Allah, I did not kill, nor did I participate in his blood.' He (peace be upon him) will say, 'Yes, you mentioned My servant so-and-so, and that escalated until he was killed, and his blood fell upon you.'

key_terms.قَدْرُ مِحْجَمَةٍ: The measure of a cup (hijama cup)

ai.seo_question: How is indirect responsibility for killing judged on the Day of Resurrection in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia concept of 'indirect causation' (sababiyyah) in bloodshed, where a single mention or influence can trigger a chain of events leading to death, thereby incurring the killer's blood debt. It highlights the spiritual weight of social influence, illustrating that accountability extends beyond direct action to include the ripple effects of one's words and status in the eyes of God.
